name: Acne
short: A common skin condition involving spots and pimples, often linked to oil glands.
overview: Acne occurs when hair follicles become clogged with oil and dead skin cells. It commonly appears on the face, back, and chest, especially during adolescence, and can also affect adults.
care: See a doctor or dermatologist if acne is severe, painful, spreading, leaving scars, or affecting wellbeing.
red_flags: Sudden severe acne with fever or feeling unwell
Signs of skin infection such as spreading redness, swelling, or pus with fever
diagnosis: Usually assessed by visual examination of the skin; tests are rarely needed.
management: Gentle cleansing, avoiding picking spots, non-comedogenic products, and pharmacist or clinician advice on suitable treatments.
ayurveda: Traditional Ayurvedic texts associate skin eruptions with imbalances involving heat and blood; traditional routines emphasize diet, digestion, and cleansing practices alongside qualified guidance.
evidence_note: Some traditional herbs have been investigated in small studies for skin-related outcomes; evidence varies and is not conclusive.
safety: Patch-test topical preparations; stop use if irritation occurs.
interactions: Topical herbals may interact with prescribed skin treatments; check with a pharmacist.
pregnancy: Topical gentleness matters; discuss any new preparation with a clinician.
children: Mild routines preferred; supervise young children.
elderly: Skin may be more sensitive; introduce products gradually.

name: Bronchitis
short: Inflammation of the airways of the lungs, often following a cold or flu.
overview: Bronchitis involves inflammation of the bronchial tubes. Acute bronchitis often follows a viral respiratory infection and usually improves within weeks; persistent symptoms need review.
causes: Irritants such as smoke or dust
care: Seek care if cough lasts more than three weeks, breathing is difficult, there is blood in mucus, or fever is high or prolonged.
diagnosis: Based on symptoms and examination; sometimes chest X-ray or breathing tests.
management: Rest, fluids, avoiding smoke, and clinician advice; antibiotics are not routinely needed for viral cases.
ayurveda: Traditional systems describe cough and chest congestion through concepts of respiratory balance; warm fluids, steam inhalation, and traditional herbs are commonly referenced alongside care.
evidence_note: Some herbs have been studied for cough-related outcomes in small trials; results are mixed.
safety: Honey must not be given to infants under one year.
interactions: Herbal preparations may interact with prescribed medicines.
pregnancy: Discuss herbal teas and preparations with a clinician.
children: Avoid honey under 12 months; gentle measures preferred.
elderly: Watch for breathlessness; seek care promptly.

name: Constipation
short: Difficulty passing stools or less frequent bowel movements than usual.
overview: Constipation means stools are hard, dry, or difficult to pass. It is often linked to diet, fluids, activity, or medicines, and usually improves with routine measures.
care: See a clinician if constipation is new and persistent, there is blood in stools, unexplained weight loss, or severe pain.
diagnosis: Usually based on history; examination or tests if warning signs exist.
management: Fibre-rich foods, fluids, regular activity, and toilet routine; laxatives only as advised.
ayurveda: Ayurvedic tradition links regular elimination with digestive balance; traditional preparations such as Triphala are classically referenced for bowel regularity under guidance.
evidence_note: Triphala has been investigated in small studies of bowel function with mixed results.
safety: Persistent symptoms need evaluation rather than prolonged self-treatment.
interactions: Laxative-type herbs may interact with medicines affecting fluids or minerals.
pregnancy: Constipation is common; discuss any remedy with a clinician.
children: Diet and fluids first; clinician advice for medicines.

name: Dengue
short: A mosquito-borne viral illness common in tropical regions.
overview: Dengue spreads through the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes. Many cases are mild, but some develop warning signs needing urgent hospital care.
causes: Bite of an infected Aedes mosquito
risks: Living in or visiting tropical areas
care: Seek medical care promptly for suspected dengue; go urgently with warning signs.
diagnosis: Clinical assessment plus blood tests where available.
management: Medical supervision, rest, fluids, and fever care as advised; avoid aspirin and NSAIDs unless a clinician advises.
ayurveda: Traditional approaches emphasize fever care, hydration, and rest; specific herbal claims for dengue lack robust evidence and must not delay medical care.
evidence_note: No well-studied herbal treatment for dengue; traditional use only, with medical care essential.
safety: Warning signs need hospital care immediately; herbs never replace that.
interactions: Avoid blood-thinning-type preparations unless advised.
pregnancy: Mosquito protection essential; urgent care for fever.
children: Watch fluid intake and warning signs closely.

name: Eczema
short: Dry, itchy, inflamed patches of skin that come and go.
overview: Eczema (atopic dermatitis) causes dry, itchy, inflamed skin. Triggers vary and flares can be managed with skin care and clinician guidance.
causes: Triggers such as soaps, heat, or allergens
risks: Family history of eczema or allergies
care: See a clinician if eczema spreads, is infected, disrupts sleep, or does not improve with basic care.
red_flags: Pus or yellow crusts with worsening pain
Rapid swelling of face or eyes
diagnosis: Clinical examination and history; allergy review sometimes.
management: Moisturizers, gentle bathing, trigger avoidance, and prescribed treatments as advised.
ayurveda: Traditional views connect chronic skin sensitivity with internal balance; diet, stress routines, and gentle herbal oils are traditionally referenced.
evidence_note: Small studies of topical herbals exist; results are preliminary.
safety: Avoid scratching; patch-test new preparations.
contra: Broken infected skin for unproven topicals
interactions: Herbal topicals may interact with steroid creams; ask a pharmacist.
pregnancy: Prefer simple moisturisers; discuss actives with a clinician.
children: Common in children; gentle care and clinician review.
elderly: Very dry skin needs regular moisturising.

name: Fever
short: An elevated body temperature that can occur with many different illnesses and conditions.
overview: Fever is a rise in body temperature above the usual range, most often a sign the body is responding to infection. The number alone matters less than the overall picture, especially in children and older adults.
care: Seek care for very high or prolonged fever, fever with worrying symptoms, in infants, or when unsure.
red_flags: Fever with stiff neck or confusion
Rash that does not fade under pressure
diagnosis: Temperature measurement plus assessment of cause; tests depend on context.
management: Fluids, rest, comfortable temperature, and fever care as advised by a clinician or pharmacist.
ayurveda: Ayurvedic tradition describes fever (jwara) with attention to digestion and rest; light diet, fluids, and traditional herbs such as Tulsi and Giloy are classically referenced alongside care.
evidence_note: Traditional use for fever support; modern evidence for fever reduction is limited.
safety: Treat the cause, not only the number; warning signs need prompt care.
interactions: Herbal teas are generally mild but check with medicines.
pregnancy: Fever in pregnancy deserves prompt clinician advice.
children: Age-appropriate dosing guidance from a clinician or pharmacist.

name: Gastritis
short: Inflammation of the stomach lining, often causing upper abdominal discomfort.
overview: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining. It can be short-term or long-term and is often linked to infection, medicines, alcohol, or bile reflux.
care: See a clinician for persistent pain, vomiting blood, black stools, weight loss, or difficulty swallowing.
diagnosis: History and examination; sometimes endoscopy or H. pylori testing.
management: Avoiding triggers, smaller meals, limiting alcohol and NSAIDs, and clinician-advised treatment.
ayurveda: Traditional digestive concepts emphasize eating habits and agni (digestive capacity); herbs such as Amla and Liquorice are traditionally referenced for stomach comfort under guidance.
evidence_note: Preliminary studies on some herbs for digestive comfort; not conclusive.
safety: Ongoing symptoms need investigation rather than indefinite self-care.
interactions: Herbal preparations may affect stomach acid medicines.
pregnancy: Common discomforts; clinician advice before remedies.

name: Headache
short: Pain or pressure in the head, with many possible causes.
overview: Headaches range from tension-type discomfort to migraine and other causes. Most are not dangerous, but certain patterns need urgent assessment.
care: Seek care for sudden severe headache, pattern changes, or headaches with neurological symptoms.
red_flags: Headache with fever and stiff neck
Weakness, vision loss, or speech difficulty
diagnosis: History and examination; scans only when warning features exist.
management: Rest, fluids, stress and sleep habits, and clinician or pharmacist advice on pain relief.
ayurveda: Traditional head-care routines include oil application (shirodhara-type concepts under practitioner care), routine, and calming herbs; evidence is traditional.
evidence_note: Peppermint oil has small studies for tension-type headache; evidence limited.
safety: Red-flag headaches need emergency assessment, not home measures.
interactions: Check pain-relief combinations with a pharmacist.
pregnancy: Many painkillers restricted; clinician advice needed.

name: Influenza
short: A contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses.
overview: Influenza (flu) spreads through coughs, sneezes, and close contact. Most people recover within two weeks, but some groups face higher complication risk.
care: Seek care for breathing difficulty, chest pain, dehydration, or flu that improves then worsens.
diagnosis: Clinical assessment; rapid tests where available.
management: Rest, fluids, isolation while contagious, and clinician advice; vaccination is the main preventive measure.
ayurveda: Traditional seasonal routines emphasize immunity-supporting diet and herbs such as Tulsi, Giloy, and Chyawanprash-type preparations; vaccination and medical care remain primary.
evidence_note: Traditional immune-support use; modern flu-specific evidence limited.
safety: High-risk groups should seek early advice; herbs do not replace vaccination or care.
interactions: Check herbal combinations with prescribed medicines.
pregnancy: Higher risk; early clinician contact and vaccination advice.
children: Watch fluids and breathing; clinician guidance.

name: Jaundice
short: Yellowing of the skin and eyes, signalling an underlying liver or bile issue.
overview: Jaundice is yellowing caused by a buildup of bilirubin. It is a sign, not a disease, and always deserves medical evaluation to find the cause.
care: Seek prompt medical evaluation for any new jaundice; urgently with confusion, bleeding, or severe pain.
red_flags: Jaundice in a newborn with poor feeding
diagnosis: Examination plus blood tests and imaging as needed.
management: Treat the underlying cause under medical supervision; rest and alcohol avoidance commonly advised.
ayurveda: Traditional liver-supportive herbs such as Bhumi Amla and Kalmegh are classically referenced; they complement, never replace, diagnosis and care.
evidence_note: Early laboratory and small clinical work; not established treatment.
safety: Jaundice always needs proper diagnosis first.
interactions: Liver-active herbs may interact with medicines; clinician review needed.
pregnancy: Prompt evaluation essential.

name: Kidney Stones
short: Hard mineral deposits that form in the kidneys and may cause severe pain.
overview: Kidney stones form when minerals crystallize in urine. Small stones may pass unnoticed; larger ones can cause intense flank pain and need care.
care: Seek urgent care for severe pain, fever with urinary symptoms, vomiting preventing fluids, or inability to urinate.
diagnosis: History, urine tests, and imaging such as ultrasound or CT.
management: Fluids, pain relief as advised, and urology follow-up; procedures depend on size and position.
ayurveda: Traditional urinary-supportive herbs such as Gokshura and Varuna are classically referenced for urinary comfort under qualified guidance.
evidence_note: Traditional urinary use; modern stone-specific evidence limited.
safety: Severe pain or fever needs urgent care, not home measures alone.
interactions: Diuretic-type herbs may affect fluid and mineral balance.
pregnancy: Imaging and treatment choices need specialist input.

name: Laryngitis
short: Inflammation of the voice box causing hoarseness or voice loss.
overview: Laryngitis inflames the larynx, often after viral infection or voice strain. Most cases settle within two weeks with voice rest.
care: See a clinician if hoarseness lasts more than three weeks, breathing is noisy, or swallowing is difficult.
diagnosis: History and throat examination; laryngoscopy if persistent.
management: Voice rest, fluids, humid air, avoiding smoke and shouting.
ayurveda: Warm fluids with honey and ginger, and voice rest, are traditionally recommended for throat comfort.
evidence_note: Soothing traditional use; limited modern trials.
safety: Persistent hoarseness needs examination, not prolonged silence alone.
interactions: Mild; check with prescribed medicines.
pregnancy: Gentle measures preferred.

name: Migraine
short: Recurring moderate-to-severe headaches, often with nausea and sensitivity.
overview: Migraine is a neurological condition causing headache attacks, often with nausea and sensitivity to light and sound. Attacks vary in frequency and triggers.
causes: Not fully understood; involves brain signalling and blood vessel responses
Triggers such as stress, sleep changes, or hormonal shifts
care: See a clinician for new, changing, or frequent attacks, or if attacks disrupt life.
red_flags: Headache with fever and stiff neck
New weakness, vision loss, or speech problems
diagnosis: History and pattern review; scans only for warning features.
management: Trigger tracking, regular sleep, stress habits, and clinician-advised acute and preventive options.
ayurveda: Traditional head routines, oil therapies under practitioner care, and calming lifestyle measures are referenced; evidence is traditional.
evidence_note: Small studies on peppermint and ginger for headache-related symptoms; limited.
safety: Red-flag headaches need emergency care.
interactions: Check combinations with migraine medicines.
pregnancy: Many migraine medicines restricted; specialist advice.

name: Neuropathy
short: Nerve damage often causing numbness, tingling, or pain in hands and feet.
overview: Peripheral neuropathy involves damage to nerves outside the brain and spinal cord. Diabetes is a common cause; symptoms often start in the feet.
care: See a clinician for spreading numbness, weakness, foot sores, or falls.
red_flags: Loss of bladder or bowel control
diagnosis: Examination, blood tests, and sometimes nerve studies.
management: Treat the underlying cause, foot care, pain strategies as advised, and safety against burns and injuries.
ayurveda: Traditional nerve-supportive routines include oil massage (abhyanga) concepts and herbs such as Ashwagandha under guidance; evidence is traditional.
evidence_note: Traditional supportive use; modern neuropathy evidence limited.
safety: Protect numb areas from heat and injury; foot checks matter in diabetes.
interactions: Herbal sedative-type products may add to drowsiness.
pregnancy: Cause-specific specialist care.

name: Osteoarthritis
short: Wear-and-tear joint condition causing pain and stiffness.
overview: Osteoarthritis involves gradual cartilage changes in joints, commonly knees, hips, hands, and spine. Activity, weight habits, and clinician guidance help manage it.
care: See a clinician for persistent pain, locking, swelling, or reduced function.
red_flags: Hot red swollen joint with fever
diagnosis: History, examination, and sometimes X-ray.
management: Staying active, weight habits, heat/cold, physiotherapy, and clinician-advised pain options.
ayurveda: Traditional joint care includes oil massage, gentle movement, and herbs such as Shallaki (Boswellia) and Guggul under guidance.
evidence_note: Boswellia and turmeric extracts have small trials for joint comfort with mixed results.
safety: Supplements never replace movement and weight care; check interactions.
interactions: Joint herbs may interact with blood thinners and diabetes medicines.
pregnancy: Clinician advice before any supplement.
elderly: Balance activity with rest; fall safety.

name: Psoriasis
short: A long-term skin condition with scaly patches, linked to immune activity.
overview: Psoriasis causes skin cells to build up into scaly patches, often on elbows, knees, scalp, and lower back. It comes and goes and needs clinician-guided care.
causes: Triggers such as stress, infections, or skin injury
care: See a clinician for spreading patches, joint pain, or impact on daily life.
diagnosis: Skin examination; sometimes biopsy.
management: Moisturisers, prescribed topicals, light therapy or systemic options as advised.
ayurveda: Traditional skin-purification routines, diet attention, and herbs such as Neem and Turmeric are referenced; severe cases need medical care.
evidence_note: Preliminary topical studies; not established treatment.
safety: Avoid harsh scrubbing; patch-test new preparations.
interactions: Check with prescribed topicals.
pregnancy: Many psoriasis medicines restricted; specialist advice.

name: Q Fever
short: A bacterial infection spread from farm animals, often flu-like.
overview: Q fever is caused by Coxiella burnetii, often linked to livestock contact. Many cases are mild and flu-like; some need antibiotic treatment.
causes: Breathing dust contaminated by infected farm animals, especially around birthing
care: See a clinician for prolonged fever after animal contact; mention the exposure.
red_flags: Signs of heart valve infection in at-risk people
diagnosis: History of exposure plus blood tests.
management: Clinician-prescribed antibiotics when indicated; rest and follow-up.
ayurveda: No specific traditional treatment; general fever-care and rest traditions apply alongside medical treatment.
evidence_note: Bacterial infection needs medical treatment; herbs supportive at most.
safety: Antibiotics as prescribed; complete the course.
interactions: Standard medicine checks apply.
pregnancy: Higher complication risk; early care.

name: Ringworm
short: A contagious fungal skin infection causing ring-shaped patches.
overview: Despite the name, ringworm is a fungal infection (tinea), not a worm. It spreads by skin contact and shared items, and usually responds to antifungal care.
care: See a clinician or pharmacist if widespread, on scalp or nails, or not improving.
diagnosis: Visual examination; sometimes skin scraping.
management: Antifungal creams as directed, hygiene, and avoiding sharing personal items.
ayurveda: Traditional antifungal-type herbs such as Neem and Tea-tree-adjacent oils are referenced; established antifungal treatment remains primary.
evidence_note: Neem has laboratory antifungal activity; clinical evidence limited.
safety: Complete the antifungal course; keep areas clean and dry.
contra: Steroid creams without advice (may worsen fungus)
interactions: Minimal for topicals; check tablets with pharmacist.
pregnancy: Pharmacist advice for antifungal choice.

name: Sinusitis
short: Inflammation of the sinuses causing facial pressure and congestion.
overview: Sinusitis inflames the air spaces around the nose. Most cases follow colds and settle within weeks; persistent or severe cases need review.
care: See a clinician if symptoms persist beyond 10–12 days, worsen after improving, or include high fever or vision changes.
diagnosis: History and examination; imaging rarely needed.
management: Saline rinses, fluids, steam, and clinician advice; antibiotics only for selected bacterial cases.
ayurveda: Traditional nasal care (nasya concepts under practitioner care), steam, and herbs such as Tulsi are referenced for sinus comfort.
evidence_note: Comfort-focused traditional use; limited modern trials.
safety: Eye or vision symptoms need urgent care.
interactions: Decongestant limits apply; pharmacist advice.
pregnancy: Saline measures preferred; clinician advice.

name: Tonsillitis
short: Inflammation of the tonsils causing sore throat and swallowing pain.
overview: Tonsillitis is usually viral and settles within a week. Bacterial cases (such as strep) may need specific treatment.
care: See a clinician for difficulty swallowing fluids, breathing difficulty, drooling, or symptoms beyond a few days.
red_flags: Severe one-sided throat pain with fever
diagnosis: Throat examination; strep testing where indicated.
management: Fluids, rest, pain relief as advised, and antibiotics only for confirmed bacterial cases.
ayurveda: Warm salt-water gargles, honey-ginger fluids (age-appropriate), and Tulsi preparations are traditionally used for throat comfort.
evidence_note: Soothing traditional use; limited modern trials.
safety: Breathing or swallowing difficulty needs urgent care.
interactions: Check pain-relief combinations.
pregnancy: Gentle measures; clinician advice.

name: Ulcerative Colitis
short: A long-term bowel condition causing inflammation and ulcers in the colon.
overview: Ulcerative colitis is an inflammatory bowel disease affecting the colon and rectum. It follows flare and remission patterns and needs specialist care.
causes: Immune-mediated inflammation; exact cause not fully known
care: Specialist (gastroenterology) care for diagnosis and flares; urgent care for heavy bleeding or severe pain.
diagnosis: Colonoscopy with biopsies, blood and stool tests.
management: Specialist-prescribed treatment plans, nutrition support, and flare monitoring.
ayurveda: Traditional bowel-care concepts exist, but active flares need modern specialist care; herbs only as adjuncts under joint supervision.
evidence_note: Early small studies on adjuncts; not established treatment.
safety: Never adjust prescribed bowel medicines based on app content.
interactions: Herbal adjuncts may interact with immunosuppressants; specialist review.
pregnancy: Preconception and flare planning with specialists.

name: Vitiligo
short: Loss of skin pigment causing light patches.
overview: Vitiligo occurs when pigment-producing cells stop working, creating light patches. It is not contagious; sun protection and dermatology guidance matter.
causes: Autoimmune pigment-cell loss in most cases
care: See a dermatologist for diagnosis, treatment options, and sun-care planning.
red_flags: Rapid widespread change with other autoimmune symptoms (needs workup, not emergency)
diagnosis: Skin examination, sometimes with Wood's lamp or biopsy.
management: Sun protection, camouflage options, and clinician-advised medical or light treatments.
ayurveda: Traditional pigment-supportive herbs such as Bakuchi (Psoralea) are classically referenced under strict practitioner supervision due to sun-sensitivity effects.
evidence_note: Early studies on Bakuchi exist; photosensitivity risk requires supervision.
safety: Sun protection essential; never use photosensitizing herbs casually.
interactions: Check with dermatology treatments.
pregnancy: Treatment choices need specialist input.
elderly: Skin cancer checks for changing spots remain important.

name: Whooping Cough
short: A contagious bacterial cough with a characteristic whoop sound.
overview: Whooping cough (pertussis) causes severe coughing fits. It is most dangerous in infants; vaccination is the key protection.
care: Seek prompt care for suspected cases; urgently for infants with apnoea, poor feeding, or blue colour.
diagnosis: Clinical pattern plus laboratory tests.
management: Clinician-prescribed antibiotics where indicated, isolation, and supportive care; vaccination prevents most cases.
ayurveda: Traditional cough-soothing measures may comfort, but bacterial illness needs medical treatment and vaccination prevention.
evidence_note: No herbal substitute for antibiotics or vaccination.
safety: Infants need urgent assessment; do not delay care.
interactions: Standard medicine checks apply.
pregnancy: Vaccination in pregnancy protects newborns; clinician advice.
children: Highest risk group; vaccinate on schedule.

name: Xeroderma
short: Abnormally dry skin, often from barrier or environmental causes.
overview: Xeroderma means excessively dry skin. Common causes include weather, harsh soaps, and skin conditions; regular moisturising usually helps.
care: See a clinician if dryness is severe, cracked and bleeding, infected, or linked to a wider rash.
red_flags: Cracked bleeding skin with spreading redness and fever
diagnosis: Examination and history; underlying cause review.
management: Gentle cleansers, lukewarm water, regular moisturisers, and humid air.
ayurveda: Traditional oil massage (abhyanga) with sesame or coconut oil is classically recommended for dry skin.
evidence_note: Moisturising traditional use; limited trials.
safety: Avoid very hot water and fragranced products on cracked skin.
contra: Severe cracked infected skin for unproven topicals
interactions: Minimal.
pregnancy: Simple moisturisers preferred.

name: Yellow Fever
short: A mosquito-borne viral illness; vaccination prevents it.
overview: Yellow fever spreads via infected mosquitoes in parts of Africa and South America. Most cases are mild, but severe cases need hospital care; one vaccine dose gives long protection.
risks: Travel to endemic areas without vaccination
care: Seek care for fever after travel to endemic areas; vaccination before travel is essential.
diagnosis: Travel history plus laboratory tests.
management: Supportive hospital care for severe cases; no specific antiviral; prevention by vaccine and mosquito control.
ayurveda: No specific traditional treatment; general fever-care traditions apply alongside medical care and vaccination.
evidence_note: Vaccination is the proven protection; no herbal substitute.
safety: Travel vaccination is essential; do not rely on herbs for prevention.
interactions: Standard checks apply.
pregnancy: Travel advice needed; vaccine decisions with clinician.

name: Zika
short: A mostly mild mosquito-borne virus with pregnancy risks.
overview: Zika spreads mainly through mosquito bites. Most infections are mild, but infection in pregnancy can harm the baby, so prevention matters most.
causes: Bite of an infected Aedes mosquito; sexual transmission possible
care: Seek care for symptoms after travel, and preconception/pregnancy counselling if exposed.
diagnosis: Travel and exposure history plus laboratory tests.
management: Rest, fluids, and symptom care; no specific antiviral; mosquito protection prevents spread.
ayurveda: No specific traditional treatment; general rest and fluid traditions apply alongside medical guidance.
evidence_note: Supportive care is the standard; no herbal substitute.
safety: Pregnancy prevention and counselling are the priority.
interactions: Standard checks apply.
pregnancy: Avoid travel to outbreak areas if possible; urgent counselling if exposed.
